newsitem.title: UK: UK'S FTSE 100 ENDS SLIGHTLY UP, BROADER INDEX FIRM.
newsitem.headline: UK'S FTSE 100 ENDS SLIGHTLY UP, BROADER INDEX FIRM.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE 100 ends slightly up at second highest close
ever. FTSE 250 surges on interest rate, sterling outlook.
** Market shrugs off weak Wall St, Treasuries start. Dow off
23 pts at London close, yield on U.S. 30-year bond rises.
** BT ends down nearly 9 pct as stock goes ex-dividend.
Britain's leading share index ended slightly higher on Monday, while the broader market powered to a five-month peak on a favourable outlook for UK interest rates and sterling.
The FTSE 100 finished up 0.6 point at 5,031.9, clawing back from a one percent selloff at the open to post its second highest closing price ever.
Volume was thin by 1534 GMT at 605.6 million shares, with advancers leading decliners by 58 to 41.
The FTSE 250 of second-tier stocks, heavily influenced by industrial companies, gained 21.1 points or 0.45 percent to 4,671.6, its strongest since March 18.

"I think the idea of interest rates being on hold for the time being is factored in, and for us to go further now will be based on individual earnings reports," said Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe.
He added, "We probably have more to go on the exporters, if sterling stays at these lower levels."
UK corporate directors and fund managers, meanwhile, signalled different opinions on the market's outlook.
British fund managers raised their cash levels in July for the first time in a year amid expectations that global stock markets would fall in the next three months, new evidence shows.

A survey conducted by Gallup for investment bank Merrill Lynch between August 4 and August 6, a day before the Bank of England raised official interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent, showed that fund managers continued to favour gilts over British stocks.
Gallup asked 68 leading British institutions controlling funds of 1.093 trillion pounds ($1.7 trillion) about their outlook for the economy and their asset allocation plans.
UK shares regained their footing, after tracking the near two percent sell-off in the Dow industrials on Friday.
"We've seen this kind of pattern before, where a sharp reaction in New York entails a brief reaction in the morning and then a more rational analysis comes into play," Monson said.
"That analysis reflects the optimism from the BOE (Bank of England) comment last week that they may have done enough for the time being," in raisingtes, he said.
That analysis was reinforced on Monday after the the release of what the market deemed benign UK producer price data for July.
The data showed the price of goods leaving factory gates remained dormant in July. Output prices rose just 0.2 percent, leaving them only 1.4 percent higher than a year ago.
In individual share activity, stocks trading ex-dividend accounted for about 28 points off the leading FTSE index, including BT going ex a special dividend.
BT shares fell 38p to 388-1/2p on turnover of 15.8 million.

Shares in UK building materials group Redland Plc resumed their recovery, leading a sector rally amid growing perceptions that UK interest rates and sterling have their seen their peaks, dealers said.
Redland shares finished up 7p at 313-1/2p, RMC gained 17p to 11.22 stg, and Wolseley 7p to 495-1/2p.
In its London Stock Exchange debut, shares in printing machinery supplier Fairfield Enterprises Plc ended at 117-1/2p, a premium to its issue price at 115p. The stock hit a 120p high.

United Utilities shares gained 9p to 710p, with brokers setting price targets of 750-760p for the stock after recent weakness. The market is now looking beyond the current fracas over executive chairman Sir Dennis Pitcher.
On Tuesday, Q3 figures are due from BOC Group Plc and H1 results are also due from General Accident Plc.

UK retail price data for July are due at 0830 GMT Tuesday. A Reuter poll of economists showed annual retail price inflation is expected to have crept higher last month, pushing the underlying rate further above the government target of 2.5 percent. The poll produced a consensus forecast that RPIX rose 2.8 percent in the year to July, up from 2.7 in June.
The headline inflation rate is expected to break above three percent, to 3.1, for the first time since end-1995.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4366
